newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-SMITH BLASTS PLAYERS OVER VIOLENCE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMITH BLASTS PLAYERS OVER VIOLENCE.

text.p: Australia coach Greg Smith rebuked New South Wales and Queensland on Tuesday for tarnishing rugby union's image by their violent on-field conduct in a spiteful Super 12 encounter on Saturday.
Three players were suspended for their part in several ugly clashes that marred Queensland's 26-16 victory at the Sydney Football Stadium on Saturday.
"I just don't think we need to promote that sort of behaviour because we need to market our sport..and you can't market something through negative behaviour," Smith said.
"I'm sure the players who are involved regret what they've done and I'm sure it won't happen again," he said.
Australian Rugby Union chief executive officer John O'Neill has described the players' conduct as an embarrassment to the sport.
Queensland hooker Brendan Cannon was suspended for 15 weeks on Sunday after being found guilty of stomping on the head of opposition winger Alistair Murdoch.
New South Wales forward Richard Harry also earned a three-week ban for kneeing an opponent, while Queensland prop Dan Crowley was banned for two weeks for fighting.
Cannon's ban was the longest handed out by a Super 12 disciplinary panel since the inception of the southern hemishphere provincial competition last year.
Three other players were reported to the disciplinary panel over incidents in the ill-tempered match but their charges were dismissed.
